title: [R3-UI leaf] Expose unavailable navigation reasons accessibly
description: SPIDR prerequisite leaf for parent task-2c952438c41546b3a736623f3956c778. Objective: make the already-fail-closed unavailable Approvals destination honestly discoverable by accessible name without inventing route or approval authority. Deliverable: NavRail conditionally includes “not available yet” in the button’s content-derived name and exposes the literal existing unavailability reason while preserving disabled/no-navigation semantics, reason description/title, SOON or daemon badge text, and responsive accessibility. Exact owned paths (3): apps/control-room/src/v2/shell/nav-rail.tsx; apps/control-room/src/v2/cordum-shell.test.tsx; apps/control-room/src/v2/styles/cordum-shell-responsive.test.tsx. NOT in scope: shell-routes/model, CordumApp, CSS, parent journeys, approval state, route enablement, manifests, or any aria-label replacement that drops badge counts. The parent’s unchanged tests/e2e/control-room/journeys.spec.ts is the served-build consumer and parent dependsOn this row. Exact verification command: pnpm --filter @moe/control-room exec vitest run src/v2/cordum-shell.test.tsx src/v2/styles/cordum-shell-responsive.test.tsx
definitionOfDone: Red-first, a direct CordumShell fixture supplies an Approvals destination with route:null and literal NAV_DESTINATION_NOT_BUILT, then asserts the production button is found by role/name /Approvals.*not available yet/, is natively disabled, exposes that exact reason code and mapped description/title, and cannot call the supplied navigator; the pre-fix assertion fails specifically because the phrase is absent from the accessible name.

NavRail adds the honest unavailability phrase only for a non-null reason inside the existing content-derived button name, retains aria-label absent, preserves item labels plus SOON/daemon count content, title, aria-describedby, active/available destinations, and no-navigation behavior, and remains below 250 physical lines.

The responsive asserting consumer remains explicit: narrow layouts never remove the nav label/badge from the accessibility tree, daemon counts remain in the button name, and an unavailable Approvals control retains both its count/SOON context and the honest phrase.

Tracked-path mutation drills remove only the conditional unavailable phrase and swap only the rendered literal reason code; the exact name assertion and exact code assertion respectively go red while disabled/route-null fences remain intact, then separate restore plus hash/diff proof returns all three tracked paths to their pre-drill bytes.

Run standalone/unpiped control-room typecheck, the exact focused verification command with nonzero Test Files/Tests counts, the full @moe/control-room test lane with nonzero counts, and root pnpm typecheck/pnpm test as merge-base-versus-HEAD path-attributed baselines; no new failure may intersect the three owned paths and foreign red is disclosed verbatim.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Selected the smallest presentation-only change at the existing NavRail seam: append an exact conditional “not available yet” phrase inside `.cr2-navlabel` and expose the already-resolved reason through a data attribute. Rejected `aria-label` because the responsive contract intentionally keeps the name content-derived so a SOON chip or daemon-authored count stays in the accessible name. Rejected changing `NAV_UNAVAILABLE_LABELS`, `NAV_UNAVAILABLE_REASONS`, or `BUILT_NAV_ROUTES` because the route roster and explanation are already correct and changing their exported shape/vocabulary would create unrelated fan-out. Rejected CSS-hidden new markup because the existing responsive `.cr2-navlabel` treatment already keeps label content in the accessibility tree; the honest phrase may be visible on the wide rail.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Measured at HEAD cb0be9e03a94a8a2b718a9f08e368eabb8013b55 with exact-path `git status --porcelain`: nav-rail.tsx (167 lines), cordum-shell.test.tsx (214), and cordum-shell-responsive.test.tsx (159) are tracked and clean. `nav-rail.tsx` resolves missing destinations fail-closed to `NAV_DESTINATION_NOT_BUILT`, sets native disabled, removes navigation for route:null, and exposes the mapped explanation through title plus aria-describedby, but its content-derived name is only `Approvals SOON`. `shell-routes.ts` already resolves Approvals to route:null/reason NAV_DESTINATION_NOT_BUILT and maps that code to the exact sentence `This destination is not built yet in this release.`; no refusal layer exists. Shape grep found the responsive test’s hard assertions that aria-label is null and badge text remains button content, so it is in the owned roster even if only assertions change. Current focused unit lane is green at 2 files/26 tests but misses this name contract; the unchanged parent CR-J1-002 served-build journey ran 1 Playwright test and failed finding `/Approvals.*not available yet/`, while its snapshot showed a disabled `Approvals SOON` button. Moe searches found no live task owning any of the three paths. Parent task-2c952438c41546b3a736623f3956c778 is structurally BLOCKED on this leaf (and the separate bootstrap leaf); a governor request is pending to mirror that relationship in dependsOn after the architect-role authorization defect refused set_task_dependencies.
planningNotes.risks: Do not convert this presentation fix into route authority: Approvals must remain route:null, disabled, and without an onClick. Do not add aria-label or hide/remove the badge, because either can erase daemon-authored counts from the computed name. Add the phrase only for non-null reason so Goals and other available/active names remain byte-for-byte in behavior. Pin the literal reason code from the rendered production button rather than iterating the resolver roster. The direct divergence fixture supplies an explicit destination plus navigator, avoiding bootstrap, legacy-root, graph, missing-handler, and other downstream fences; removing only the phrase must leave disabled/route-null behavior intact yet redden the named assertion. Preserve foreign Control Room dirt and touch only the exact three clean paths.
